item: The background briefing rebuild keeps its Thread handle and writes the cache where it started; a conftest fixture joins briefing threads after each test
summary: R333. service._refresh_thread holds the oo-briefing-refresh Thread (set under _refresh_lock, stays set after it ends; is_alive() says whether it runs); _ensure_background_refresh resolves the cache path once, before taking the lock, and the thread pins it in a ContextVar that _cache_path() reads in that thread alone, so every cache read and write of the run goes to the folder it started in (before: data_dir() at each use, so a thread that outlived its test wrote briefing_cache.json into a later test's OO_DATA_DIR, the 25,847 B file R332 found). refresh_briefing's signature is unchanged. tests/conftest.py gains an autouse _briefing_threads_quiesced that joins live oo-briefing-refresh / oo-briefing-bg threads for at most 30 s in all after each test and fails that test's teardown naming the thread and the test id for a survivor; tests/test_briefing_background_handle.py pins the handle (found without threading.enumerate), the start-time path (red first: mutated to ignore the pin, the cache lands in the moved folder), and the quiesce (joins, fails naming both, ignores other threads). Stated limits: shutdown.py joins no named thread, so no shutdown step was added; warm_cache and _dismissed_path resolve their own paths. Not measured: how long a real rebuild takes on a large corpus.
